paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD does not leave His people in the ditch. Jerusalem drained the cup of His fury to the dregs, and the prophet says that among all her sons there was no one to take her hand (Isa 51:17-18). Then the LORD, who defends His people, says, "See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering." He says she will never drink from it again (Isa 51:22). That's the God we serve, and He does the lifting Himself.

Notice what the LORD asks of her in return. Nothing! He says, "You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed" (Isa 52:3). Friend, I've been marked down to 25 cents, and even I know you can't pay your way out of a hole like that. The LORD does the redeeming, and she only has to wake up, shake off her dust and put on her garments of splendor (Isa 52:1-2). That's still how it works today, so if you feel stuck, lean in and hear Him say it to you.

And the news is so good that somebody has to run and tell it. "How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, 'Your God reigns!'" (Isa 52:7). He doesn't send His people out the door in a panic, either, because "the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard" (Isa 52:12). He's out in front and He's right behind you, so you can walk out of that dark place with your head up. This story isn't over, friend, so keep that oven warm.
